Codelco chairman addresses Chamber committee on production inconsistencies and transparency measures
Codelco Chairman Bernardo Fontaine addressed a parliamentary commission regarding inconsistencies in company production figures. He outlined ongoing investigations and reaffirmed commitments to transparency while emphasizing rigorous processes for public disclosure.
The Chairman of the Board of Directors of Codelco, Bernardo Fontaine, said on Oct. 7 that the corporation's administration will address inconsistencies detected in production figures with determination and transparency before the Special Investigating Commission of the Chamber of Deputies.
Fontaine told the parliamentary body that after detecting an initial case of overproduction, company-initiated reviews led to identifying a second case under investigation, where production figures were doubled between two divisions. He said the administration is committed to addressing these cases and any new findings “with determination and transparency, without delays, without corporate defenses, without trying to protect people, areas or decisions simply because they belong to Codelco.”
Fontaine explained that investigations must focus both on identifying individual responsibilities and understanding process or control failures that allowed such discrepancies. “It is not enough to find those responsible. We also have to correct what allowed these events to occur. And if it is determined that Codelco suffered financial losses, our mandate is to use all available instruments to pursue their restitution,” he stated.
He emphasized rigor in publicly releasing information due to Codelco’s economic and social significance. “Being transparent also means being rigorous. We cannot transform hypotheses into certainties, anticipate responsibilities, or establish figures or potential damages before they have been properly determined. This does not diminish our commitment to fully clarify these events; it compels us to do so with greater rigor,” Fontaine said.
Fontaine added that multiple bodies are examining these cases—including internal investigations by Codelco itself as well as external audits by entities such as the Comptroller General of the Republic and Public Prosecutor’s Office—reinforcing his call for careful procedures at every step.
He concluded by linking this response with a broader goal: “Our mission is to return Codelco to an undisputed leadership position in its industry... That means recovering production... but also strengthening confidence in our management.” Fontaine was accompanied at the session by several vice presidents and managers from across Codelco.
